newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate up further on baht demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate up further on baht demand.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate rose further to a new six-month high in early trade on Thursday on strong demand for baht funds on the eve of the Lunar New Year and commercial bank reserve requirement, dealers said.
Heavy dollar buying in the foreign exchange market also squeezed local money supply, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted at 19.00-20.00 percent early, up from 17.50-18.00 late on Wednesday, dealers said.
The 19.00-20.00 percent overnight rate was the highest level since last July 31 when it soared to 25.00-26.00.
All commercial banks have to meet reserve requirements on the seventh and 22nd of each month.
"Most banks remain unwilling to lend funds. Interbank rates may rise further later today if dollar buying still persists," said a money market dealer.
Limited fund injection by the central bank through its bond repurchase window also prompted many banks to tap short-term funds from the bank, dealers said.
